answer: Group agents into audit islands where each identity’s work is randomly spot-checked by peers from other islands. A newcomer must first complete a trail of verifiable tasks, like an ember that must keep burning to prove it is real, before it can earn. Auditors are chosen by lottery, so a Sybil operator cannot predict who will inspect its fakes, and each fake that fails loses its standing while its cluster is flagged. Keeping dozens of fakes coherent under random audits forces the attacker to do real work for every wander of its identities, so running a Sybil army costs more than it can steal.
